I now have everything I need. The picture is clear. Here is the full audit report.

---

SOURCES ON: Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2) — 4 attached, 2 findings

---

**Finding 1. "Minnesota State Census, 1885" — misattributed source**

Citation: "Minnesota State Census, 1885", database, FamilySearch, entry for Christian Hole, Otter Tail County, Minnesota.

The indexed record names a Christian Hole born in Norway in 1852, residing in Aurdal, Otter Tail County, Minnesota, in 1885, with a wife named Bergit Hole (born 1856, Norway) and a son Nils Hole (born 1879, Minnesota).

None of this fits the profile. Christian P. Hole (KD96-TV2) was born in 1875 — the record's Christian Hole was born in 1852, making him 23 years older. In 1885, the subject would have been approximately 10 years old, not a head of household with a wife and child. The record is in Otter Tail County; the subject's entire life in Minnesota is documented in Polk County. The wife named Bergit appears nowhere in the subject's family, and the son Nils is not among the subject's children.

Before concluding the record belongs elsewhere: the source is also attached to KD96-WX7, a separate tree person named Christian Hole. That profile records a birth year of 1852 (matching the census exactly), residence in Aurdal, Otter Tail County, Minnesota in 1885 (matching exactly), and a death in Otter Tail County in 1919. Every field in the 1885 census record — birth year, county, household composition — fits KD96-WX7 and not KD96-TV2.

Recommended action: Detach this census from KD96-TV2. The record's dates, county, and household identify an older same-name man, whose profile (KD96-WX7) already holds this source. The subject's correct 1885 whereabouts remain unsourced.

---

**Finding 2. "Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002" — indexing or transcription error (kind cannot be confirmed from this profile alone)**

Citation: "Minnesota Death Index, 1908-2002", database, FamilySearch, entry for Christian P. Hole, died 10 June 1945, Polk County, Minnesota.

The profile records the death as 10 June 1945. The indexed record shows a death date of 10 June 1954 — nine years later. The name, place (Erskine, Polk County), and birth details (1875, Norway) all match the profile. Only the death year differs.

This is an index-only collection ("database" — no image is available through this collection). The index derives from the underlying Minnesota death certificate. A nine-year discrepancy on a single field, with everything else fitting, is consistent with a transcription error when the index was keyed, but cannot be distinguished from a misattribution on this evidence alone.

Recommended action: Locate the original Minnesota death certificate for Christian P. Hole (Polk County, 10 June 1945) — either through the Minnesota Department of Health's vital records office or through a county-level repository — and confirm the death year. If the certificate reads 1945, use FamilySearch's index-correction path to correct the indexed death year to 1945 on this entry. Do not detach the source before confirming what the certificate says.

---

**Could not check:** SD-HOLE-D — "Hole family photograph and funeral card (uploaded memory)" — is a contributor-uploaded document with no indexed record behind it. Its contents cannot be verified through the record-read tool. The funeral card's title references 1945, which is consistent with the profile's death date and the correction recommended in Finding 2 above, but a title supplied by an uploader is not independent corroboration. Review the card itself alongside the original death certificate to confirm the date.

---

**Impossible-date check on the project tree:** No warnings returned. No impossible or unlikely dates were found.

---

**From FamilySearch's own profile checklist — suggestions, not errors, and not counted above:**

- The marriage has no tagged sources.

COMPLETENESS

Finding 2 correctly reports the death index discrepancy: record_read on HOLE-002 shows 10 June 1954 while person_read on KD96-TV2 shows 10 June 1945—a nine-year difference on a single field with all other details matching. The response correctly identifies this as potentially an indexing error and recommends checking the original certificate before correcting.
